subject: geom_bar - discrete x axis with multiple values per group

messages.author: 68fb7536659cabae
messages.subject: geom_bar - discrete x axis with multiple values per group
parts:
Hi everyone,

I'm trying to create a barplot with a discrete axis but I was wondering if it is possible to group multiple values together.
This is what I have so far:

df <- data.frame(items = c(1,1,2,2,2,4,4,4,3,5,6,7,8,9,10,10))
ggplot(data=df, aes(factor(df$items))) +
  geom_bar(breaks=c(1,3,4,7,10),
           col="red") +
  labs(y="Count")

Which result in the following graph. I tried using breaks, which works fine in geom_histogram but does not seem to work for my barplot.
Any ideas how I can group them together? For example values 1-3 in bar one, 4-7 in bar two...

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: geom_bar - discrete x axis with multiple values per group
parts:
It's not easy to dodge bars without some common aesthetic by which to group them, but one can facet and then "remove" the facet backgrounds. An ugly hack, but it appears to do the job.

items = c(1,1,2,2,2,4,4,4,3,5,6,7,8,9,10,10)

library(plyr)

 # generate a frequency table as a data frame. sorted by item
DFrq <- count(items)    
# manufacture a vector that groups items together, add to data frame
DFrq$grp <- rep(1:3, c(3, 4, 3))

library(ggplot2)

# theme_minimal gets rid of most of the background elements,
# including panel borders. The theme() call is designed to make
# the strip text (values of grp) 'disappear' from the display as
# well as the x-axis ticks. The vertical major grid is sufficient.

ggplot(data=DFrq, aes(x = factor(x), y = freq)) + 
  theme_minimal() +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "red", color = "black", width = 1) +
  labs(x = "Item", y="Count") +
  facet_wrap(~ grp, nrow = 1, scale = "free_x") +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(colour = "transparent"),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank())

Hope this is close to what you wanted...
Dennis

messages.author: 942ffec526d6a312
messages.subject: Re: geom_bar - discrete x axis with multiple values per group
parts: Jos,

> Thank you for your answer Dennis, unfortunately it is not exactly what I
> was looking for. In your answer the values are indeed nicely grouped
> together but they are still in separate bars. If possible I would like
> them in one bar. Is that possible?

It's easier. You can use cut (see ?cut for help) to create a
factor with your required grouping, and then plot that:

df$fitems<-cut(df$items,breaks=c(0,3,7,10),labels=c("1-3","4-7","8-10"))
ggplot(data=df, aes(factor(df$fitems))) +
geom_bar(breaks=c(1,3,4,7,10),col="red") +labs(y="Count",x="Items")

Ron.
